zh.title: 逆运动学
summary:
1、逆运动学的两种求解方式：
     ✅ 解析闭形式解（analytic closed‑form）：通过建立机器人运动学方程，利用代数方法求解关节角度。
     ✅ 迭代数值解法（iterative numerical methods）：通过迭代优化算法，逐步逼近目标位姿的关节角度解。
     ✅ 解析法的优点：
			计算速度快，适合实时控制。
			可以得到所有可能的解，便于选择最优解。
			对于结构简单的机器人，解析法通常是首选。
     ✅解析法的缺点：
			对于结构复杂的机器人，解析法可能无法得到闭式解。
			需要对机器人结构有深入理解，推导过程复杂。

✅数值法的优点：
			适用于各种结构的机器人，包括复杂的多自由度机器人。
			可以处理冗余自由度和约束条件，灵活性高。
			可以结合优化目标，如最小化关节运动、避障等。

✅数值法的缺点：
			计算速度较慢，可能不适合实时控制。
			可能收敛到局部最优解，需要良好的初始值和迭代策略。
			需要设置收敛条件和步长参数，调试复杂。
     ✅ 记住：真实机器人 IK 迭代，误差是误差旋量，不是简单位置相减。

2、普通伪逆 IK 的致命缺陷：
     ✅ 当机器人靠近奇异位形时，雅可比矩阵 J 接近降秩。此时使用普通伪逆 J† 求解会得到巨大的关节增量 Δθ，容易导致关节角度突变，最终使迭代过程发散。

3、阻尼最小二乘法 DLS（Damped Least Squares）：
     ✅ 优化目标中加入正则化惩罚项，在减小末端位姿误差的同时限制关节增量不能过大。
        min ‖𝒱_{e} − JΔθ‖² + λ²‖Δθ‖²
     ✅ 求解公式：
        Δθ = J^{T}(JJ^{T} + λ²I)^{-1}𝒱_{e}
     ✅ 阻尼系数 λ 的作用：
        • 远离奇异位形时，λ 几乎不起作用，求解效果接近普通伪逆，精度较高。
        • 靠近奇异位形时，λ 能抑制过大的关节增量，使末端精度略有损失，以换取更好的数值稳定性。
        • λ 不能设置得过大，否则阻尼过强会造成收敛困难，并使残余误差无法消除。

4、工程版数值逆运动学的完整流程：
     ✅ 输入目标位姿 T_{sd} 和关节初始值 θ_{0}。
     ✅ 进入迭代循环：
        ① 正运动学：根据当前关节角 θ^{i} 计算末端当前位姿 T_{sb}(θ^{i})。
        ② 计算相对变换 T_{eb}，通过对数映射得到误差旋量 𝒱_{e}。
        ③ 判断误差是否足够小；若满足收敛条件，则退出循环。
        ④ 计算雅可比矩阵 J，并使用阻尼伪逆求解关节增量 Δθ。
        ⑤ 更新关节角：θ^{i+1} = θ^{i} + Δθ，然后返回循环起点。
     ✅ 输出迭代收敛后的关节角。

5、数值 IK 的三个固有短板：
     ✅ 强依赖初值：当初始关节角距离目标解过远时，算法可能收敛到其他解，甚至无法收敛；工程轨迹通常使用上一时刻的关节角作为当前迭代初值。
     ✅ 目标位姿超出机械臂工作空间时，算法无法收敛。
     ✅ 阻尼系数 λ 通常需要根据机器人状态和任务需求手动调节。

en.title: Inverse Kinematics
summary:
1. Two approaches to solving inverse kinematics:
     ✅ Analytic closed-form solutions: formulate the robot's kinematic equations and solve for the joint angles algebraically.
     ✅ Iterative numerical methods: repeatedly update the joint variables to approach a configuration that achieves the target pose.
     ✅ Advantages of analytic methods:
        • Fast computation, making them suitable for real-time control.
        • All possible solutions can be obtained, allowing the most appropriate one to be selected.
        • Usually the preferred approach for robots with relatively simple kinematic structures.
     ✅ Limitations of analytic methods:
        • A closed-form solution may not exist for robots with complex structures.
        • They require a deep understanding of the robot's geometry, and the derivation can be complicated.
     ✅ Advantages of numerical methods:
        • Applicable to many robot structures, including complex systems with many degrees of freedom.
        • Able to handle redundancy and constraints, providing greater flexibility.
        • Additional objectives such as minimizing joint motion and avoiding obstacles can be incorporated.
     ✅ Limitations of numerical methods:
        • Slower computation may make them unsuitable for some real-time control tasks.
        • They may converge to a local solution or fail to converge, so a suitable initial guess and iteration strategy are important.
        • Convergence criteria, step sizes, and other parameters must be selected and tuned.
     ✅ Key point: in iterative IK for a real robot, pose error should be represented as an error twist rather than a simple difference between position vectors.

2. A critical limitation of standard pseudoinverse IK:
     ✅ When the robot approaches a singular configuration, the Jacobian J becomes nearly rank-deficient. Solving with the standard pseudoinverse J† can then produce an excessively large joint update Δθ, causing abrupt changes in the joint angles and potentially making the iteration diverge.

3. Damped Least Squares (DLS):
     ✅ A regularization term is added to the objective so that the end-effector pose error is reduced while excessively large joint updates are penalized.
        min ‖𝒱_{e} − JΔθ‖² + λ²‖Δθ‖²
     ✅ Solution:
        Δθ = J^{T}(JJ^{T} + λ²I)^{-1}𝒱_{e}
     ✅ Effect of the damping coefficient λ:
        • Far from singular configurations, λ has little influence, so the solution remains close to the standard pseudoinverse and retains high accuracy.
        • Near a singular configuration, λ suppresses excessively large joint updates, trading a small amount of end-effector accuracy for improved numerical stability.
        • λ should not be set too high; excessive damping can slow or prevent convergence and leave a nonzero residual error.

4. Complete engineering workflow for numerical inverse kinematics:
     ✅ Inputs: the desired pose T_{sd} and an initial joint configuration θ_{0}.
     ✅ Iterative loop:
        ① Forward kinematics: use the current joint configuration θ^{i} to compute the current end-effector pose T_{sb}(θ^{i}).
        ② Compute the relative transformation T_{eb}, then apply the matrix logarithm to obtain the error twist 𝒱_{e}.
        ③ Check whether the error is sufficiently small; exit the loop once the convergence criterion is satisfied.
        ④ Compute the Jacobian J and use the damped pseudoinverse to solve for the joint update Δθ.
        ⑤ Update the joint configuration: θ^{i+1} = θ^{i} + Δθ, then return to the beginning of the loop.
     ✅ Output the converged joint configuration.

5. Three inherent limitations of numerical IK:
     ✅ Strong dependence on the initial guess: if the initial joint configuration is too far from the desired solution, the algorithm may converge to a different solution or fail to converge. In engineering trajectories, the joint configuration from the previous time step is commonly used as the next initial guess.
     ✅ The algorithm cannot converge when the target pose lies outside the robot's reachable workspace.
     ✅ The damping coefficient λ usually needs to be tuned manually according to the robot's state and the requirements of the task.
